Pretty fun game, lots of replayability
Love it and can´t wait to see what the devs will do in the future

I liked it for the first 10 hours and I feel like the game was designed to be fun for roughly that amount of time. Afterwards, everything felt very generic. The Meta-Progression doesn't feel rewarding or interesting, It's always the same, build some production chain, resolve the same events over and over.

Not neccessarily a bad game, but not a good roguelike.

This review is long overdue for this fantastic title. I'm not always the biggest fan of rogue-likes; I usually go for never ending Paradox strategy games, but the basic gameplay loop here is just so perfect, and the meta-game is sufficiently interesting and challenging, that I keep coming back for more, even when I put the game down for a month or a year... If you're into rogue-likes, RTSs or turn-based strategy, just buy the game, you'll love it.

Bad help system. Controls that don't work right and don't give proper feedback. Structure and resource type spam, and building one of each becomes a hoop in a series you need to jump. Where's the game part

Updated Review - Feb 15, 2026 - 44.1 hrs :
I've had a lot of fun with this game, it has kept me coming back over and over, and I would say this game now deserve a spot in my top favorites. But I will say the game progression has slowed down a bit, and after playing 40 maps over and over, it started to get a bit less fun. I will be putting the game down for a while, and I think this is one I will be coming back to.

Feb 3, 2026 - 11.3 hrs:

If you’re looking for a game that runs on literally anything but looks like a polished gem, this is it. Against the Storm is a masterclass in optimization. The low-poly graphics are clean and vibrant, avoiding the grainy "retro" look while staying lightweight.

The gameplay is a brilliant mix of city management and roguelite progression. It gives me major Warcraft 3 nostalgia, not because it plays exactly like it, but because it captures that same "magic" in the atmosphere. Highly recommended for anyone who wants a strategy game that feels fresh yet familiar.

This has been the best city building game I have played in forever. It has an early settlers vibe, but with so much character and life to it that you must play more.

You build up your town and win through gaining prestige. Though there is a timer called "impatience" that sets the clock for you - achieve certain objectives, make your people happy and your prestige increases.

The exploration and opening glades is nervewracking and has a risk/reward feel - you dont know what you will get, but if you have the goods to solve it you reap great rewards.

Love it, have played it a lot and it continue to get better with each update.

It's... okay. I played a couple of times a couple of years ago, and just can't bring myself back to playing it again. So I guess I'm going to give it a thumbs down, since I don't want to play it again.

A video game that scratches a "They are Billions" itch, and it's like Scythe had a baby with Starcraft; but no combat. Just looming dread that the forest will force all of your workers insane.

You're technically racing "the Queen's impatience", but mostly it's the madness.

-----

Update, one beef that I hope the devs address for other folks:
On a cycle you play 6 or so games, 10ish hours of effort. A big goal is to reach a seal, which is like a boss level.

There's a warning when you try to enter that I believe said I was "early". I was not and the level was ended prematurely on my twice, messing up the work of 2 runs :(

I ran out of time twice, when all I needed was more time.

I think that message needs to be more clear, and it shouldn't say things like "early". Very frustrating to avoid the last level because of that message and get cut off.

It could quantify how many seasons until the end, but 'early' was a dirty lie that I should have ignored.

Wow, this game is really fun! Always cool to see developers experiment with genre and make something new.

Everything in this game is great: the music is nice, the gameplay - while complex - is immensely rewarding and deep, and the roguelite elements mean you can have some REALLY GOOD meaty bite-sized gameplay sessions.

This is a really good podcast game too. Even though it has stressful moments, it can also be relaxing.

It's not a perfect analogy, but "Frostpunk turned into a rogue-like" does a pretty decent job of describing the basic idea of this game.

Have citizens.
Put citizens in buildings.
Buildings do stuff.
Stuff makes your numbers go up.

You get it.

I'm going to play 1,000,000,000,000 hours of this game

A true hidden gem.

The best aspects of colony building and roguelite mixed into a tasty stew.
There are a lot of mechanics, but they all work together really nicely to make a game with a lot of run variation and room to optimise.

Lots of difficulty scaling so you can set your preferred experience. Higher prestige levels force you to minmax more and more, which is appropriate. If you play in the mid prestige, you'll have a lot of room to experiment without being punished too hard for not playing completely optimally.

There's so much going on here that it's hard to talk about in one review.
if you like colony building games and roguelites, there is no reason to not get this. The DLCs are fine, they mainly add more variety in races and biomes. They are slightly pricey, but the game is so good I got them both day one.

Incredible city builder game for me, someone who is somewhat of an outsider to the genre. Has great tutorials to get you up to speed, and ends up being intuitive rather quickly. Really fun going through the layers of progression between your overall career level/tree, each cycle of settlements, and then where you actually play the game with all the settlements. Interweaves nicely and always feels fresh with the roguelike/dynamic approach to win/loss conditions. Highly recommend

A great game i can fully recommend.
The game has a good base difficulty, and lets you seek out increasing challenge from the start if you want to.
The roguelike aspects are well done, and the game organically guides you towards more and more difficult playthroughs.
10/10 in its genre. great game, fully recommend.

Neat little city builder game - random quests, different biomes and races and having to pick your building blueprints amongst the randomly suggested ones adds variety to the game, keeping it fresh for a while. Even then, building a settlement, expanding it until it thrives and then abandoning it only to do it all again will undoubtedly get stale sooner or later.

This game is a marvellous gem fo banished-like city builder maniac like myself. A huge breath of fresh air to game design, balancing, on the edge quest tracking and of course difficulty. Against the Storm will restore your faith in gaming industry!

Rogue-like strategy city builder with almost never ending content. It's also almost a puzzle game by way of different ressources found that are transmutable into different things.
Can't believe i poured 80 hours into this already. It may be a bit repetitive but thats it's biggest flaw really.
Would recommend it to anyone. I hate bat people now though.

8.5/10.

Awesome worldbuilding, consistent gameplay that I can always know that I'm signing up for an awesome experience every time. I love how smooth and well polished the game mechanics are. The art style is a good interesting. My wife and I play this all the time, our feel good game!

Against the Storm focuses on the best part of a city builder which is the first hours when you are in the building phase. Against the Storm plays out differently every time because the buildings you start with are always different. It is a well optimized game, with constant choices of risk vs reward, and enjoyable when you figure out work-arounds for meeting necessary resources, through supply chain management.

What I appreciate about Against the Storm is that there is never is a point where it gets too complicated with too much too deal with at one time. The equivalent of the "Boss battle" is challenging and rewarding. Graphic and sound design are excellent.

I've played >1,000 hours and still not sick of it, so there must be something to this video game.

Support these devs. Eremite Games is a Polish developer consisting of six, and they really have created a real gem of a game, and they have been actively improving and polishing the game for more than a year after the day 1 release.

So I passed the tutorial just fine, but lost the first few games. There is a slight learning curve, and it takes a while to catch on. Once you do catch on, you won't stop playing. It is very addicting. The graphics are beautiful, the music is peaceful, to the point you want to take a nap. I've been very impressed with this game. Make sure you upgrade your settlements perks in the citadel. I had a harder time as I progressed because I didn't realize they were there.

Love this game and recomend it strongly.
However there is a massive letdown regarding the meta progression. Which is unfortunate as thats one of my favorite mechanics when in base builder and RTS games.
So you ether have key mechanics locked behind these uppgrades or like 1% cheaper trading or something trivial. So that and receving relativly little of the recources in relations to how long the rounds are, made me stop playing to get to the end and instead no w i just play it casual when i feel like relaxing, not caring for recources, gates, difficulty, or the world at large.
And thats a shame as i think this could have been my all time favorite game if they just had nailed that last part.

It a very good, deep, and well designed city builder. I highly recommend it with a "but".

But...

- It's not for you if you want to build a large, sprawling city. Most of time as soon as you get your settlement all tidy up (usually 1-2 hours) it's time to move on anew.
- It's not for you if you want to take your time, relax, and build. Resource are very limited and there's constant pressure from different elements: the weather, the queen, time, dangerous events... etc. That will keep you on your toes and you have to react on the spot.
- It's not for you if you want pretty graphics. The art design is okay, but many buildings looks very similar and looks like a game from 10 years ago.

A very nice game, it's technically a city builder, but it plays more like a RTS game where your enemy is resource management and decision making against various timers, and not timers in a normal sense where they limit you, but rather a check whether your build is good all around. It's also a roguelite, the gameplay loop is basically you pick a tile on the strategy layer, that tile is a match, the tile has various bonuses and negatives, then once you win that tile you expand outwards, once enough time has passed based on wins/losses the strategy map is reset and you restart stronger with the bonuses you've earned the last expedition, to go further.
Citybuilder but with a game loop behind it. A must-play if regular city builders are a little too chill for you.
Good fun. Bit of a time sink, it keeps going from daylight to dark outside whenever I play this.

Combining city-builders/worker management with rogue-lite gameplay was an inspired choice. You never hit the part of city building where you've clearly won, there are no further problems, and it's boring. That's when the run ends, typically.
Do you like fun? If you like fun this is game for you. If you like sleep or being able to keep track of time and commitments, probably steer clear of this one.

You figure how it works in first few runs. Then it is just the same game loop for all other runs.
The problems is there very little thing to do and there is very little that you can control.

Basically, it is just use the resource on the map to build product to fulfill the missions. There seems to many different types of item but they are similar items with different skin.

The game loop heavily depends on the resource on the map and there are nothing you can do if that resource is not available. You just build whatever the missions needs and win. There is no strategy really involved.
The skill tree does not feel important. Most of them are just changed the stats for a few percentage.

I bought this game after reading a review saying "buy this game when you like city builder games but you always start a new city instead of sticking with one" and I have to say that this was good advise.
Outside of not having to feel guilty for never building the perfect city over the course of many many hours it also offers a beautifully crafted fantasy world with a nice soundtrack, intriguing lore and cool visuals.
I enjoyed every hour spent with this game so far, even when my village didn't succeed, even though I tend to get easily frustrated.

Bought this on a whim cause I thought the artwork looked nice, and I'm really glad I did.
It's a very fun roguelite spin on the city builder genre. I'm pretty casual at this genre and I found it quite approachable.

I would call this a rogue like city builder and for someone who loves city builders and rogue likes it reaaaallllly scratches that itch so well. It's the type of game you can sit down for one round or ten rounds and it's extremely satisfying.

The art is distinct and lovely. The soundtrack is great. Gameplay feels thoughtful and well balanced.

There are a lot of ways you can play, which is super nice. It keeps things refreshing. Lots to unlock, it's easy to reset everything once you feel you've squeezed all you can out of a save. Would love to see this come to the switch so I can take it on the go (at least until I can splurge on a steam deck).

Really great strategy game that avoids the mid/late game management slump with its cycle mechanic. You get the fun of building new settlements with different challenges while also slowly building up progress over time to get credit for perks that will allow you to handle increasingly difficult scenarios. The developers listen to their community and haven't been afraid to take risks as well as add large quality of life improvements along with bug fixes.

If you're a fan of city building and/or management games, this is for you. Each settlement you build will be different thanks to the roguelite elements of the game. You never know what building and bonuses you will get, or what you will find on the map, and this forces you to adapt your strategy on the fly. Highly addictive!

Against the storm is a city builder game with roguelite elements. Your goal is to build settlements to collect resources for the Queen. Instead of there being regular enemies, you instead break into forest glades which contain random events, resources, and other nodes in order to expand your city and win the game. You gain in game currency to unlock permenant buildings and upgrades, which is nice and keeps the game fresh. The rate at which you gain new blueprints and other things is also pretty good.

Overall it's a fantastic game already and I can't wait until it comes out fully. The devs are responsive and update known issues quickly.

Great take on the city-builder genre, with plenty of good updates and constantly listening to the community and incorporating feedback into the game. It is essentially a city-builder rogue-like where you build up multiple successive settlements and it feels fresh each time you build your settlement. I rarely submit reviews but this game deserves it and it's definitely worth your time.

The most unique and original survival city-builder game I've played. Very high replayability value offers many long hours of fun, very interesting world setting that works fantastically with the game mechanics. A game more than worth its full price.

If you want a classic city-builder experience and build one settlement and stop when you're bored, you can do that with all the cards and map effects you want! Otherwise the main gameplay loop involves building a settlement and accumulating reputation as quickly as you can within a time limit. The faster you do, the better, and once you do, you move on to the next settlement and have to try to make as many as possible within a single game "year". Works way better than it sounds, and if you don't wanna lose progress and wanna keep playing the map, you can.

What can I say, this games a gem. It's not my usual kind of game, but I grew up on age of empires and its got that similar charm.
The art style is gorgeous. The gameplay variation is endless. The detail and depth of the game just keeps you engaged and learning each time you play. It is alot to learn and pick up and can be overwhelming but stick with it, because this game is addictive.

Against the Storm is fantastic! If you like RTS games or city-builders, or you just like a game with tremendous personality, attention to detail, and love put into it; then this is the game for you. The developers put out updates often that are largely based on community feedback. The game has a large learning curve, but it also have many tools to help out new players. For more experienced players, it has many difficulty modes and extremely difficult challenges to conquer. The soundtrack for the game is also stellar. Buy this game to support indie developers who love gaming and know how to make a great game!

Damn, this game is good

The best part of most city builders is the beginning portion, when you're struggling to make ends meet and developing a strategy to keep your city going. Once you've laid a foundation and get into the macro/passive parts, the city feels done, even if it isn't. This always leaves me with a lack of satisfaction and direction on what to do next. Against the Storm solves that issue by forgoing the macro altogether. Once you get your city fully settled, the game ends either with a victory or defeat, meaning the beginning, superior micro stage is the *only* stage.

Every settlement will also be slightly different. You'll have access to a different set of buildings, resources and population each time you play, meaning your entire approach and strategy needs to be different as well. It's so engaging to take your ragtag group of settlers and figure out how to make your limited pool of options work.

I highly recommend this game.

Very fun rogue-like builder game, but the RNG absolutely sours the whole dish. While I understand the point of the game is to have a different run each time, it is endlessly frustrating simply never being able to find the resources absolutely needed to run the city because of RNG. Need clothes for your citizens or else they'll all leave, but never find any cloth-related nodes simply because of RNG, or a blueprint to make them because of RNG, which ends a hours-long run? It's not fun. It's not engaging. It's just losing a game/wasted time because the game refused to offer you what you needed because of dumb luck, which is not good or fun gameplay.
Honestly have found a lot of fun in this game, but at the end of the day it's impossible to ignore the fact the RNG becomes an absolute impassible concrete wall at times as opposed to a passable challenge/hurdle it should be, considering the delicate balance of everything required at higher levels/deeper in.

PS - new update with frogs just makes issues worse. Foxes have mostly worthless traits (finding water even though they can't benefit from it anymore?) Harder to keep complex food needs met. Still issues where some necessary basic ingredients to make bricks or cloth simply don't exist outside of RNG.

Insanely addicting game that understands that the best part of a city builder is the initial setup and reaching a point where it self-sustains enough to achieve certain goals. You have finite resources as well as a soft time limit and need to work out how to please your villagers, fulfil orders/missions and gain the reputation needed to "complete" the settlement. Once completed you quit out and do it again, only this time you'll have a different biome, different resources, different villager species, different map modifiers, so on and so forth. The roguelite elements are well implemented and the Prestige system adds plenty of increasing difficulty.

After 26 hours of that game already, I can attest it some very addictive elements. Also looking at the roadmap, I am pretty sure this game will satisfy me for an even longer period without getting old. I don't know if i ever played a game comparable in the composition of genres. Combining city building, eco-sim and rogue elements is quite refreshing to me! Thanks to the developers for an awesome addition to my steam library! 10/10

A roguelite citybuilder is not something that should work this well and yet somehow it does.

Even as things are being tweaked and adjusted, there's already a really fun balance between the many recipes and builds you can do (everything has alternates so if the RNG hates you, you can still make do with some creativity), so every town you make feels like its own unique challenge and is engaging in different ways.

It's a game that somehow manages to be very chill (The art direction! The music! The incredibly asmr-ish pitter patter of the rain!) and very stressful (The timed events! The unseen monarch tapping their foot disapprovingly! The many ways to absolutely mangle your production lines!) at the same time and yet makes it work.
The runs are short enough that you don't feel terrible when you lose, but long enough that you still get that city-builder satisfaction of watching your towns grow.

There's still things missing on the roadmap, but this already feels like a complete game and is an easy recommend.

The best rogue-like strategy I've ever played!
Hate and at the same time love this game!
Definitely worth trying, especially if you a fan of base building or city sim games!

P.S. It's a great example of west-style economy: "You have an issue - throw money in it! Money fix everything!"
This game gets updated every two weeks and doesn't charge you for DLC packs for it. There's no reason to not buy this game, it really is a labor of love. Hands down best 2023 game in this category.

This game is amazing.

For quite a while now, I have have not been generally able to enjoy gaming as much as I did...

This game made me not sleep the whole night, made me dream about it, woke up and realized that the reality of this game is even better than my dream.

In my humble opinion, this game is great.

Now back into the storm!

This is by far the best early access game I ever played.

Constant updates + already contents enough to make other games at release feel shame.

Bare in mind this is by no mean a city builder, it's not a relaxing game at all. It's a rogue-lite with an extremely high skill ceiling, where you will have to slowly refine your strategy to literally utillize all resources presented to you to survive. You're not looking for a long-term survival, exploit everything and achieve win conditions by any means possible quickly.

The best part of any strategy game is setting up your base. This is all that. It has a wonderful progression where games get longer when you are ready for them, and you can ignore the more complicated mechanics at first and ease your way into them.

Sadly, it does not scratch the ich of city-builder. It's more alike to a puzzle game or eBoard Game with resource gathering designed to unblock your path forward. Comic graphic (Warcraft3-like) does not help either for me, but it's just personal taste.

It has some nice ideas like rouge-lite elements, multiple races that have different needs / strengths, but it ends up highly repetitive and lacking in simulation department.

A bit too fiddly on the Steam Deck (though doable I'm certain), works a treat on an M1 Mac with Crossover. Don't be mislead by the RTS styling and city management, this is a roguelike more similar to Slay The Spire than Age of Empires. You're going to use logistics and base building to accomplish goals and win a map so don't spend too much time getting cozy (unless thats your thing of course). I'm finding the game incredibly charming once I got past the tutorial - if you bounce off once or twice because it just doesn't seem like your jam give it another go, it reveals itself after an hour or two.

Tutorials are in the form of highly limited runs, which nearly turned me off the game forever. My friends got me to try it again, though, and now that I'm in the main game it's a lot more fun. So perservere through the tutorial.

tldr.text: Very Positive (95%): players love the challenge and the combat loop.
Complaints are few and spread across different topics, with no single problem standing out.

details.text: Gameplay complaints have ticked up only slightly in recent reviews, so a buyer now faces much the same experience as before.
Newer players are much less won over: 55% positive, against 98% among long-time veterans.
